title: Growing-Path Event-Study Width Frontiers with Rare Cohorts under Parallel Trends
banked_reason: F1.5 citation-instantiation overflow: four load-bearing probability theories absent from Mathlib/Causalean; Anderson study exhausted two bounded build windows with eight sorries and no review, so faithful Lean formalization cannot complete in this run.
gap_reasons: The generic residual is the cited results themselves: generic chaining comparison, Anderson Gaussian shift inequality, Gaussian isoperimetry and median concentration, and the CCK triangular-array hyperrectangle CLT plus Gaussian covariance comparison.
Reached BUILD_CAP (10) without the scaffolder requesting review.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery passed the field-tier D0.5 review after source citations were corrected and independently attested. F1.5 found four load-bearing probability interfaces absent from Mathlib and Causalean, so the Anderson inequality was sent to a reusable study. Two ten-round build windows produced compilable scaffolding but ended with seven and eight remaining sorries and no review; generic chaining comparison, Gaussian isoperimetry, and the CCK rectangle CLT also remain, so this is a solver/substrate block rather than a refutation of the mathematical result.
tldr: In a fixed-strata independent-panel PT-All experiment, the composition-changing event-study path has a joint information geometry rather than unrelated scalar standard errors. This experiment is narrower than the models studied by Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess, Callaway and Sant'Anna, and Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie. The covariance formula is a finite-dimensional Gaussian specialization and re-expression; the contribution begins with growing-path Gaussian-width minimax and honest-band equivalence and the resulting schedule laws. For uniform adoption, the squared frontier has the elbow \(\{(T+1)/(n(T-H))\}\log(1+\min\{H+1,T-H\})\), which yields the exact near-terminal consistency threshold. The note also gives geometric and full-path laws, a zero-comparison-mass boundary, and a computable band under condition (A), while the largest feasible region for designs not satisfying (A) remains open.
gap: Existing staggered-adoption work supplies fixed-period simultaneous bands, scalar growing-period sufficient conditions, and fixed-period efficient influence functions, but it does not determine the matching joint risk and honest-width frontier when the horizon grows and comparison cohorts shrink.
fill: The project derives the projected information covariance, matches its Gaussian width by causal upper and lower bounds, evaluates it sharply for uniform and geometric schedules, and asks exactly when a projected covariance bootstrap attains the frontier.
